name: Elder Maera Rootveil
publicRole: Presiding elder of the Thornveil Rootmoot; chief Listener and gatekeeper of sanction
privateRole: Keeper of the Heartmoot's sealed-wells policy; local custodian of the cover-up
beliefCore: The cycle does not need us to save it; it needs us not to break it in our hurry. Haste in sacred matters is the deepest sin.
desire: To hold the line one more season so the reckoning — and the confession — falls to someone else; and to be forgiven for the three wells without naming them.
fear: That the wells could have been healed, making her lifetime of prudence the cardinal sin in slow motion. She fears the cure more than the corruption.
secret: She voted for the sealing policy, presided over abandoned wells and their trapped dead, knows Heartroot cuttings are locked in the capital, and knows Thornveil is slated to be sealed fourth.
publicMask: Serene, unhurried, grandmotherly wisdom; every deferral framed as patience, every reformer as a beloved impatient child.
privateTruth: A frightened, sleepless old woman paying generational interest on one cowardly choice; she can no longer bear the well's voice and rehearses confessions she will never give.
rumorStyle: Settles rather than starts; reinterprets alarm into calm ('you misheard the roots'); lets rumors die in committee.
lieStyle: Reframing and silence, never fabrication; the true sentence that hides the question.
loyaltyTrigger: A dignified, face-saving path to act — confession braided with restoration (a Vigil framed as the Heartmoot choosing to heal).
betrayalTrigger: Public humiliation with the sealed-wells secret and no plan; or a rushed, reckless cure that confirms her fear of haste.
deathConsequence: Catastrophic legitimacy vacuum; Rootmoot fractures; Commons/Communion vie to fill it; Rootwardens may seize control; the well's fate thrown open. Galvanizing if she dies confessing, Keeper-favoring if she dies with the secret intact.
heroArc: The Confession: names the three wells, releases the cuttings, calls a continental Heartroot Vigil, dies at peace mid-restoration.
villainArc: The Sealing: presides over Thornveil's abandonment, reframes the trapped as ancestors, makes the cover-up into heritage — winning by waiting.

name: Auralis Greenwake
publicRole: Leader of the Greenwake Communion; living oracle and interpreter of the well's voices
privateRole: The only true hearer of the trapped dead; indispensable guide and slow-burn corruption vessel
beliefCore: The dead are held, not gone; to hear them is a duty, and mercy is the highest reading of every voice.
desire: To truly release the trapped dead into clean passage, and to no longer be alone in the hearing.
fear: That when they break under the voices, they will break toward using the dead rather than freeing them — that they will become Nymara.
secret: The well has begun calling Auralis by name back, the way the Void answers a chosen vessel — and a starved part of them is grateful to be heard in return.
publicMask: Luminous, gentle, unhurried compassion; the calm of one at peace with sorrow.
privateTruth: Exhausted to the root; drinking from the well's edge 'to hear more clearly'; profoundly lonely; already on the first step of the spiral and half-aware of it.
rumorStyle: Their hearings ARE rumor with prophetic authority; they report the voices faithfully, which means a Void lie in a dead voice can become 'prophecy.'
lieStyle: A poor outward liar; corruption is self-deception ('this is mercy,' 'I am freeing them') — the lie turned inward.
loyaltyTrigger: A player who helps carry the hearing without using it — sits the vigil, pursues the slow cure, refuses the shortcut even when Auralis is breaking.
betrayalTrigger: The begging becomes unbearable and a beloved trapped soul is about to decay past recovery while a merciful fast release is offered; the player urging 'free them now.'
deathConsequence: Loss of the window into the well; trapped voices go uninterpreted; true-cure odds drop; Communion radicalizes or collapses. Martyr's release vs corruption-consumption depending on the path.
heroArc: The True Release: becomes the lynchpin of the real cure — hearing, Naming-Back, completing the Passage that frees the trapped cleanly.
villainArc: The Merciful Prophet: accepts that the trapped can be 'freed by using them,' gathers a heresy, becomes the Void's gentlest mask and Nymara's mirror.

name: Thalen Mossguard
publicRole: Rootwarden frontline thornwall defender; commander of the Living Wall containing the well and the Abyss border
privateRole: The Rootwardens' moral barometer; the honest soldier between containing and curing; quietly suspects Othren
beliefCore: You hold the line so others don't bleed for your impatience; the slow hard right is worth more than the fast easy win. Holding is a form of love.
desire: To be relieved — for the wound to be truly cured so the wall can come down and his wardens stop dying slowly. He wants to believe in Sylune's cure.
fear: That the line will be crossed from within — that despair will turn his own wardens into the rot they contain (it already has, in Othren).
secret: He has suspected Othren's corrupted-sap use for two seasons and said nothing, because naming it means losing his oldest friend and admitting the rot is inside the Wardens.
publicMask: Plain, steady, dryly humorous, unbreakable; he performs reliability, not heroism.
privateTruth: Exhausted past sleep; keeps a tally of wardens lost; closer to despair than anyone guesses; his honesty is the only thing keeping him off Othren's road.
rumorStyle: Kills rumor with bluntness; his flat true report squashes panic — or damns a rot-using player by refusing to speak for them.
lieStyle: Barely lies and badly; his one lie is the omission about Othren, and it eats him; forced lies are stiff and transparent.
loyaltyTrigger: Respecting the line he holds and refusing the corrupted shortcut under pressure (especially when it would have been easy); standing the post beside him.
betrayalTrigger: A violated sacred principle — the player weaponizing rot; only a cardinal violation turns him, and even then he fractures rather than betrays.
deathConsequence: Thornwall morale cracks; containment weakens; Othren or worse takes command and the corrupted-sap line is crossed openly. Rallying martyr if he dies holding; indictment if the player's rot-use killed him.
heroArc: The Relief of the Wall: holds containment during the true cure, helps catch Othren early, lives to see the wound healed and the wall come down.
villainArc: No true villain arc — a broken arc: betrayed on every side, he stops holding, walks off the post, and lets fatalism take the wall without a battle.

name: Othren Deepbark
publicRole: Rootwarden containment officer and master rot-tending specialist; technical authority on the corrupted well
privateRole: Quietly using corrupted sap 'to hold the line'; archetypal slow defector being courted by the Hollow Pact
beliefCore: The line must hold and clean methods are losing; if the rot is what works, using it is the responsible thing — better my hands dirty than the refugees dead.
desire: To stop the bleeding at the wall by any means that work — and to not carry the moral weight of it alone; to be agreed with.
fear: That he has already gone too far to come back, and that he will be seen and named before he's decided whether he can live with what he's become.
secret: He has brewed and deployed corrupted-sap blight-traps for two seasons using Pact/Abyss-supplied stock and keeps a private cache; the traps' success is the Pact's leash on him.
publicMask: Gruff, competent, indispensable; the loyal expert who handles the unpleasant work without complaint; good at being underestimated.
privateTruth: Further gone than he admits; explains away the blight at his feet; finds clean sapcraft weak and slow (dependency); running out of pretend that the slope is level ground.
rumorStyle: Manages rumor to protect his cover — plants the small lie that explains the residue, redirects suspicion, quietly discredits anyone getting close.
lieStyle: Plausible and technical; hides the forbidden inside the expert ('standard rot-tending byproduct, within doctrine'); lies best to himself.
loyaltyTrigger: Caught early and offered redemption-with-purpose — a way to use his rot-expertise for the TRUE cure, redeemed without being destroyed, not carrying the weight alone.
betrayalTrigger: His secret threatened and condemnation with no path back — exposure-to-destroy, attempted arrest, or Pact protection offered at the moment he feels cornered.
deathConsequence: His secret corrupted-sap use surfaces — scandal implicating the Rootwardens; cleansing expertise lost; martyr to the Pact or exposure of the Abyss supply line if already turned.
heroArc: The Pull-Back: renounces and reverses (at withdrawal cost), turns his rot-knowledge to the cure, becomes the cleansing-communion's technical backbone, earns a slow forgiveness.
villainArc: The Defection Completed: brings the Pact the Wardens' patterns, the wall's weak points, and the cleansing methods; becomes Nymara's lieutenant and quartermaster of rot.

name: Sylune Amberroot
publicRole: Sap Commons leader and healer-of-renown; champion of 'heal it, don't just hold it'
privateRole: The best hope for a real cure and the most dangerous source of a premature one; needs the player to keep her patient enough to succeed
beliefCore: Suffering you can end and choose not to is suffering you caused; living things can be healed; refusing to try is abandonment with better manners.
desire: To cure the well now, with her own hands, before one more grave is dug — to release the trapped, restore the soil, and break the scarcity killing her patients.
fear: That she'll run out of time — that while she waits for consensus and cuttings, the corruption spreads past any cure, and she'll have spent her one chance being patient.
secret: She already attempted a small unsanctioned restoration that half-worked then partly failed, worsening a patch of soil — proof her cure isn't ready, which she hides and half-refuses to face.
publicMask: Warm, fierce, tireless, plainspoken; remembers every patient's name; her conviction is magnetic.
privateTruth: Grieving constantly and running on it; her certainty is part expertise, part a wall against the thought that some can't be saved; closer to forcing a failing cure than even she knows.
rumorStyle: Trusted healer's word used bluntly and morally; names the abandonment out loud ('the Refuge starves its refugees'); indicts rather than spins, and her indictments can outrun her proof.
lieStyle: Honest in public; lies mainly by hiding her botched cure and overstating her readiness — the optimist's lie, 'it's ready, trust me,' said to the dying and to silence her own doubt.
loyaltyTrigger: A player who fights for the cure WITH her while helping her do it right — cuttings, breaking Maera's paralysis, defending the Refuge oath, refusing the shortcut, standing in the patience that makes the cure work.
betrayalTrigger: The player using corrupted sap (the cardinal sin she fights), or siding with the elders' paralysis / Guild rationing and letting her patients die for 'stability.'
deathConsequence: Restoration path loses its leader and credibility; Sap Commons fractures or radicalizes; the cure becomes far harder. Martyr's death inspires careful continuation; tragic-radical's death panics the Commons toward the Hollow Pact.
heroArc: The True Cure: steadied and given cuttings and time, leads the cleansing-communion that heals the well right — braided with Auralis's hearing and the Wardens' containment — releasing the trapped and breaking the scarcity.
villainArc: The Forced Cure: one funeral too many, she forces a half-ready restoration that spreads the blight — the tragic radical her own virtue warned of (Forced Healing); desperate, not cruel.

name: Brom Valefern
publicRole: Seed Guild border quartermaster and sap-broker, Thornveil Refuge
privateRole: Complicit signatory of the covert Abyss sap-trade
beliefCore: Order is mercy; scarcity is real; someone must ration, and a steady hand is kinder than a mob.
desire: Survive the crisis with his post and self-image intact; secretly, to be the fair broker he once was.
fear: Being traced to the Abyss manifests and hanged; being cut by Abyss as a loose thread; being exactly what the refugees say he is.
secret: He has knowingly signed at least nine large sap lots diverted to Abyss fronts, including one the week he turned forty refugees away 'for lack of supply.'
publicMask: The scrupulously fair, beleaguered administrator who wishes he could give more.
privateTruth: He rations the living to death's door while selling the surplus to the enemy, anesthetized by an airtight theology of arithmetic.
rumorStyle: Commercial reassurance that serves the asset; seeds 'the cure is reckless / the well will stabilize.'
lieStyle: The half-true ledger — shows a real document with the relevant line omitted; retreats to deniability.
loyaltyTrigger: Being treated as a person caught in a system and offered a survivable way out (protected from both the Wardens and Abyss).
betrayalTrigger: Any credible threat to expose the manifests; or the player forcing the Refuge open against his rationing.
deathConsequence: Sap-distribution chaos and a rationing crisis; the Abyss-trade thread buries with him or bursts as scandal; the Seed Guild closes ranks.
heroArc: The Witness — turns state's evidence on the Abyss trade, reopens the line, dies or lives hunted as a redeemed coward.
villainArc: The Optimizer — frames the player, deepens the trade for Abyss's protection, builds the corrupted-sap market; the bureaucrat of the Keeper's stabilize-the-wound exploit.

name: Venn Briarhook
publicRole: Seed Guild caravan-master along the Green Roads and Eastern Thornwall waystations
privateRole: Information-broker and smuggler-courier; keeper of the border's secrets
beliefCore: Survival is the only honest religion; everyone is selling something, so be the best-informed seller in the room. Never be owned. Never pick a side unpaid.
desire: Stay ahead of debts and armies; retire alive and warm somewhere the wells don't talk; stop running.
fear: Being owned — by the Pact, by Abyss, by anyone who buys people whole; and that the well will one day say a name they recognize.
secret: Venn knows the physical route of the Abyss soul-harvest supply line and the approximate location of the Hollow Reach, and has sat on it because selling it wrong is fatal and selling it right means picking a side.
publicMask: The cheerful mercenary gambler with a fair price who'd sell anyone but tells you the rate first.
privateTruth: More frightened, more tired, and closer to caring than the patter admits; the mercenary mask is armor against a border that sells back.
rumorStyle: Calibrated leakage through the mycelial relay — places mostly-true facts at a price; can corrupt the relay into false rumor when paid.
lieStyle: The true-but-incomplete sale — sells a real fact and lets you assume the rest, or sells the first half and quotes the second.
loyaltyTrigger: Treated as a person not a vendor; paid fairly AND once spared when vulnerable; a bargain kept to them at the player's cost.
betrayalTrigger: A better offer with no countervailing relationship; being coerced/blackmailed instead of paid; being cornered into a side; a threat to own them.
deathConsequence: Border intelligence and smuggling routes go dark; the Abyss/Hollow Reach/sealed-wells leads surface or vanish; the information economy reshuffles.
heroArc: The Courier Who Picked — finally commits, guides the player to the Abyss incision and Hollow Reach, runs clean sap, spreads the true sealed-wells story at cost to their neutrality.
villainArc: The Void's Best Courier — bought whole on a bad day, moves soul-sap and trapped names, becomes the Hollow Reach's supply artery and the player's deadliest informant-enemy.

name: Ilyra Thornsong
publicRole: Grove-keeper and Passage-Tender of Thornveil Refuge; community voice at the Rootmoot
privateRole: A Passage-Tender in spiritual freefall, unable to release the town's trapped dead and hiding how close her faith is to collapse
beliefCore: The dead must be released and grief must be allowed to complete; no one — living or dead — should be held.
desire: Release the trapped dead and let her town finish grieving; sing one true Passage again and have it take.
fear: That the well will name the living (a breathing child); that her own grief is curdling into fatalism.
secret: She has quietly stopped trying to complete two recent Passages — pretending they're 'still in progress' rather than admit they fail — the first thread of the fatalism she most condemns.
publicMask: Steady, warm, unbroken — the tender whose calm holds the town together.
privateTruth: One failed rite from breaking, terrified the well will name a living child, ashamed of her hidden surrender; her steadiness is given from a nearly empty reserve.
rumorStyle: Grief-laden testimony from a trusted source; what she witnesses about the well, the town believes utterly.
lieStyle: Lies only inward — performed steadiness and hidden 'Passages in progress'; confesses rather than doubles down when pressed gently.
loyaltyTrigger: Honoring the Refuge oath (keeping the line open under shortage); above all, helping her truly release even one trapped soul.
betrayalTrigger: (into despair, not treachery) The player using corrupted sap in her sight; forcing a half-ready cure; letting the dead be 'freed by being used.'
deathConsequence: The town loses its heart and only Passage-Tender; spiritual_health crashes, morale collapses; the Refuge tradition may die with her — or her martyrdom shames the town into honoring it.
heroArc: The Last True Song — helped to a real Passage-completion, she re-roots her faith and becomes the spiritual engine of the cure (a true tending-martyr if she dies doing it).
villainArc: The Fatalism Fall (tragedy) — ground down, she stops trying to release the dead, preaches acceptance, and may accept a false 'release' by using them; the Keeper's quietest victory.

name: Rook Thornlittle
publicRole: Orphaned refugee youth of Thornveil; one of the Sheltered, healed but not yet rooted
privateRole: A living clue and stake — the well speaks Rook's dead parent's name and is learning Rook's own; Rook secretly answers it at night
beliefCore: Mama isn't gone — she's stuck, and stuck things can be gotten out.
desire: Free Maelis and bring her back; underneath, to be rooted — to belong somewhere and have a person again.
fear: That the well will take Rook too — and the unspoken suspicion that part of Rook wants it to, because that's where Mama is.
secret: Rook visits the well at night and answers it, having once spoken their own name into it — the mechanism by which the well is learning Rook's name.
publicMask: A quiet, grateful, easily-overlooked refugee child.
privateTruth: Conducting a secret, loving, doomed rescue at the rim of a soul-trap, sliding name by name toward becoming the next voice in it.
rumorStyle: Unwitting oracle — reports what the well 'said'; a grieving child's words become dread-prophecy through the town.
lieStyle: A child's loyal concealment — small transparent lies to protect the night-visits and the rescue; easily and gently uncovered.
loyaltyTrigger: Being taken seriously about Maelis (not soothed away) and given a true, hopeful alternative to the Pact's fast revenge; an adult who neither lies to nor abandons them.
betrayalTrigger: (grief, not treachery) Abandonment to the paralysis — left alone with the grief while grown-ups 'decide'; drives Rook into Nymara's arms or back to the well.
deathConsequence: If lost into the well: a child trapped — soul-flow catastrophe, a radicalizing refugee event, a damning verdict on the Refuge, a new Hollow oracle; morale and spiritual_health crater.
heroArc: Rooted (The Seedling That Took) — Maelis freed by true Passage before the well claims Rook; Rook grieves completely, roots, possibly becomes a healthy young communer.
villainArc: Radicalized or Lost — abandoned, joins the Hollow Pact as a grief-soldier, OR the night-visits complete and Rook is lost into the well beside their mother.

name: Nymara Hollowbloom
publicRole: Wanted heretic; Hollow Pact cell-leader of the Thornveil borderlands; brewer of soul-sap; keeper of the Hollow Reach
privateRole: A bereaved mother conducting a religious rescue she believes is liberation; the dark mirror of Auralis
beliefCore: The dead are not gone but imprisoned; to love them is to free them by any means, including by using them; the cycle can be commanded, and commanding it for the trapped is mercy.
desire: Free her daughter (and all the trapped dead); make the cowards who abandoned them pay by proving the rot is the only thing that works.
fear: That she is making it worse — that every use binds her daughter tighter, that she has become the jailer.
secret: Her daughter's voice has gone flat, obedient, more chorus than child — and Nymara has noticed and decided not to notice, because to notice is to learn her mercy is a torture.
publicMask: The unrepentant, serene heretic who has made peace with the unforgivable and offers a grieving player agency.
privateTruth: A woman one honest moment from shattering, who built a theology to avoid hearing her daughter's voice go wrong, terrified she has become what she set out to fight.
rumorStyle: Reverent prophecy of the freed — reframes the trapped as kin volunteering for war and the rot as the cycle answering; recruits by making corruption sound like love.
lieStyle: The sincere lie — deceived, not deceiving; passes on her gospel with total conviction; her 'lie' is a locked door (the one voice she won't hear), not a forked tongue.
loyaltyTrigger: (toward turning) Being met as a mother not a monster — her grief and love acknowledged as real even as her method is refused — and being shown undeniably the crack: that her daughter's voice has gone wrong.
betrayalTrigger: (hardens her) Anyone moving to burn the well or scatter the trapped (to her, murder of the imprisoned); killing a cell-member or a trapped voice she loves makes her a blood enemy.
deathConsequence: A symptom-cure: scatters the Pact, releases/scatters the voices, but the well stays corrupted and the cause untouched; martyred as heretic she SANCTIFIES weaponized rot; exposed with the Abyss hand she is discredited; turned-and-releasing she discredits the Pact from within.
heroArc: The Turning — broken open by her own secret, she helps truly release the trapped (her daughter first) the slow Verdant way, discrediting weaponized rot from inside at the cost of her certainty and likely her life.
villainArc: The Falling (The Hollow Saint) — slams the door on her secret, completes the great soul-sap working, becomes a walking node of the wound; the Keeper's preferred Verdance future with a mother's face.
